obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident reporting
trigger: A cybersecurity incident involving IT or OT systems the company operates or maintains: unauthorized access, malicious software, denial of service, a physical attack on network infrastructure, or any other incident that results in or could result in operational disruption (II.C.2.a-e). Both runbook scenarios qualify
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying the incident (II.C.3); supplemental information within 24 hours of it becoming available (II.C.5.f). IC Surface-2025-01 recommends earlier notice to TSA for significant incidents
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares the report with TSA. The report must state that it is made to satisfy the Security Directive
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - TSA-designated (P03 section 1). Reports are SSI under the directive
clock_starts: Time the company identifies a cybersecurity incident
owner: Cybersecurity Coordinator (Security Manager); alternates; shift supervisor if no Coordinator can be reached (POL-03 4.8)

obligation: PHMSA immediate telephonic notice of an incident
trigger: An incident under 191.3: a release of gas with death or in-patient hospitalization, estimated property damage of $122,000 or more (excluding gas lost; PHMSA posts inflation adjustments), or unintentional gas loss of 3 million cubic feet or more; OR an event that is significant in the judgment of the operator (191.3 paragraph (3)). A cyber-caused shutdown or curtailment may be judged significant even with no release
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery, but no later than one hour after confirmed discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - interstate transmission operator; PHMSA has direct jurisdiction. Default for a cyber-caused shutdown: report
clock_starts: Confirmed discovery: when it can reasonably be determined, from information available at the time, that a reportable event has occurred (191.3)
owner: Director of Pipeline Safety and Compliance

obligation: PHMSA revision or confirmation of the telephonic notice
trigger: An incident reported under 191.5(a)
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmed discovery, to the extent practicable: revise or confirm estimates of product released, fatalities and injuries, and other significant facts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made
owner: Director of Pipeline Safety and Compliance

obligation: PHMSA written incident report (transmission)
trigger: An incident required to be reported under 191.5
deadline: As soon as practicable but not more than 30 days after detection; supplemental report as soon as practicable when more information is obtained
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made
owner: Director of Pipeline Safety and Compliance

obligation: Emergency notice to public safety answering points and officials
trigger: A gas pipeline emergency, including a shutdown or loss of supply that creates a hazard or that local officials must plan for; any notification of potential rupture
deadline: No fixed clock for general emergencies: notify and coordinate as the emergency plan provides. Immediately and directly after receiving a notification of potential rupture (192.615(a)(8))
notify: 9-1-1 centers and fire, police, and other public officials along the route in Alabama, Georgia, and Florida
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the event creates an emergency
clock_starts: Start of the emergency or receipt of a notification of potential rupture
owner: VP Operations; controller on duty for rupture notifications

obligation: FERC posting of service outages and capacity reductions
citation: 18 CFR 284.13(d)(1); NAESB WGQ standards incorporated by 18 CFR 284.12
trigger: Any planned or actual service outage or reduction in service capacity, including a cyber-caused curtailment
deadline: No fixed clock in 284.13(d)(1): equal and timely access whenever capacity is scheduled. NAESB WGQ notice timing was not reviewed (copyrighted; P03 section 1)
notify: Informational Postings on the company website (manual posting if the customer activities website is affected), plus shipper notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - interstate pipeline
clock_starts: Time the outage or capacity reduction is known

obligation: Operations services agreement notice to lateral owners
citation: Operations services agreements with the 2 lateral owners (contract)
trigger: Loss of SCADA monitoring of an operated lateral, or monitoring that cannot be trusted
deadline: Within 30 minutes; service credits after 4 hours. Each owner makes its own regulatory notices for its lateral, and the company supplies the facts it needs
notify: Municipal gas utility lateral owner; power generator lateral owner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Shipper and interconnecting pipeline notices
citation: FERC gas tariff and interconnect operating agreements (contract)
trigger: Curtailment or shutdown affecting receipts or deliveries
deadline: Before any curtailment where possible, then every 4 hours
notify: Affected shippers (9 LDCs, 7 power plants, 22 industrial customers, 6 marketers) and the upstream interstate pipelines at the 4 receipt interconnects
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and tariff

obligation: Voluntary report to the FBI
trigger: Ransomware, extortion, or suspected nation-state activity
deadline: Voluntary; as early as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary
owner: Security Manager through the General Counsel

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
owner: General Counsel; CEO and board chair approve (POL-03 4.10)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee HR and payroll records; shipper contacts are business information)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause if provided in writing to the Department within 30 days; law enforcement delay allowed)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if employee personal information was accessed (worked example for state law)
owner: General Counsel with the HR Director

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible: 600 current employees, most in Florida, plus former employees. Count Florida residents before deciding

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Possible if former employees are included
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (HR and payroll SaaS, ERP vendor, MSSP) has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach
notify: The company (General Counsel and Security Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - tracked in contracts (STD-03)
owner: Supply Chain Manager tracks; General Counsel receives

obligation: State data breach notification (other states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (employees in Georgia and Alabama, former employees elsewhere)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay, or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
citation: Cyber insurance policy (contract; $20 million limit, $500,000 retention)
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Board and sponsor notice
citation: Board audit committee charter; PE sponsor agreement (contract)
trigger: Severity 1 incident or any precautionary curtailment
deadline: Same day for Severity 1; next quarterly meeting for others
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - governance

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief that a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment is disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered as a pipeline required to report to TSA (proposed 226.2(b)(14)(iv), as corrected by FR Doc. 2024-12084) and by size; the ransom payment report would be new

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a registered entity with high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems
deadline: Within 1 hour after determination; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a NERC-registered entity and owns no Bulk Electric System assets. The 5 power plant customers that are registered make their own decisions; the company tells them promptly of any curtailment

obligation: Form DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report
citation: Form DOE-417, OMB-approved ICR 202402-1901-002 (expires 2027-05-31); mandatory under 15 U.S.C. 772(b)
trigger: Electric emergency incidents and disturbances, including cyber events, at electric utilities and other listed entities
deadline: Emergency Alert (criteria 1-9) within 1 hour; Normal Report (criteria 10-13) within 6 hours; Attempted Cyber Compromise (criterion 14) by the end of the next calendar day after determination; System Report (criteria 15-27) by the later of 24 hours after recognition or the end of the next business day; final report within 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no electric operations

obligation: SEC cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held; no registered securities

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article found in a system used under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day (52.204-25(d)) or 3 business days (52.204-23(c)) of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
